content: Ambient audio beds in polished games use 2-4 continuous loop layers (base wind/room tone + 1-2 texture layers) plus a pool of randomized one-shot spot sounds (birds, creaks) triggered at random intervals with pitch/volume/filter variation. Repetition is avoided by breaking loops into randomized fragments and never letting one-shots settle into a recognizable pattern. On combat entry, games remove specific elements (songbirds) and/or duck the whole ambience bed to a reduced volume via a scripted state, restoring it after the encounter - contrast between exploration and combat is intentional. Sources: gameaudiolearning.com, bugnet.io, splice.com, asoundeffect.com.
